done_when: When the intake or the first round predicts more than the fix file limit, Forge asks for the size allowance at fix start or before the round; forge next lists every pending owner choice first, with its exact question and how long it has waited; new and existing repos get it on upgrade

known.title: Not done: forge next omits and mis-times pending owner choices
Publish and enforce the intake size stop across machines
Allow the owner to narrow a size-stopped fix
Exclude generated files from the predicted fix size

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done: When the intake or the first round predicts more than the fix file limit, Forge asks for the size allowance at fix start or before the round; forge next lists every pending owner choice first, with its exact question and how long it has waited; new and existing repos get it on upgrade
Case: normal use - A decision cold read or client sign-off review reaches its limit, a spec awaits confirmation, or a worker asks a question on another machine. This pass only moves blocks already present in the report. The report scans specs but not decision-read or sign-off stops (src/forge/nextstep.py:343 and src/forge/records.py:504), does not classify spec confirmation as a choice, and reads worker questions from the local record rather than the shared PR wait (src/forge/nextstep.py:1085). Those choices can be absent or buried. Also, src/forge/owner_choices.py:75 takes the first spec notes with a matching name across worktrees, so a stopped reread can show the older wait from main instead of the current branch.
findings.title: Not done: forge next omits and mis-times pending owner choices

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - One teammate starts a fix whose intake predicts six code files, and another picks it up. task._new_checkout publishes the branch before this commit (src/forge/task.py:289), but the new stop is committed only locally. The second machine therefore sees an ordinary started fix and can begin work without the allowance. Even if the stop is pushed, require_active checks the current checkout before worker.checkout picks up the remote branch (src/forge/worker.py:95), so it does not enforce that stop on first pickup.
findings.title: Publish and enforce the intake size stop across machines

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - The owner declines a size allowance and chooses a smaller result. forge fix amend calls close._worktree (src/forge/task.py:793), which calls require_active (src/forge/close.py:638). This new guard refuses the amendment itself, and the predicted-file stop remains in place. The owner cannot narrow and continue the existing fix without first granting the allowance they declined.
findings.title: Allow the owner to narrow a size-stopped fix

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 4 (floor: migration)
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A fix needs five source files and a generated migration snapshot marked linguist-generated. This count includes the snapshot, so Forge asks for an unnecessary allowance and blocks work. The actual fix limit excludes generated files in src/forge/githooks.py:230, and the first-round brief at src/forge/templates/brief.md:230 also omits that exclusion.
findings.title: Exclude generated files from the predicted fix size

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A coordinator reruns forge work or forge land from the main checkout while the size decision is pending. The refusal instructs them to run forge fix allow-large there, but that command requires the current branch to be the fix branch (src/forge/task.py:730). Following the displayed next step therefore fails instead of recording the owner's answer.
findings.title: Point the size-stop refusal at the fix checkout

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - The intake or worker prompt loses the instructions that produce the early question. Test 1 supplies File lines itself without checking the offered intake prompt, and test 3 supplies a canned question without checking that the brief says to ask it and stop before edits (tests/test_owner_choices_before_work.py:66). Both can pass while those instructions are missing. Tests 2 and 4 also check only the short round-limit phrase, not the complete question; test 2 checks that both durations occur without associating either duration with its question. They would pass with truncated questions or swapped waits.
findings.title: Gate: owner-choice command tests

why: Owner choices wait 14-55 minutes at a client: the size allowance is asked mid-round instead of at fix start, and pending owner choices are not at the top of forge next with their wording and wait time
